title: U.S. Forces Staged for Massive Iran Strikes Pending Trump’s Signal After Midterms
snippet: U.S. military assets in the Middle East are positioned to launch widespread attacks against Iranian nuclear, energy, and military infrastructure within 96 hours if President Donald Trump gives the go-ahead.
content:
WASHINGTON — American military forces throughout the Middle East are fully staged and capable of initiating a major campaign of air and missile strikes against Iran within 96 hours of a directive from President Donald Trump, according to several U.S. defense and intelligence officials.

Unlike previous limited retaliatory strikes intended to disrupt local launch capabilities, any new campaign would represent a significantly expanded operation. Defense officials indicate that leadership at U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) and the Pentagon have developed a comprehensive target list that includes key Iranian energy infrastructure, military command nodes, and nuclear facilities.

A Broader Strategic Operation

Internal Pentagon discussions suggest the administration is contemplating action far beyond routine deterrence measures. Sources familiar with internal deliberations say that while President Trump has not formally issued a final order, momentum appears to be building toward authorizing significant action, likely following the upcoming U.S. midterm elections.

The heightened state of readiness coincides with intelligence assessments indicating Tehran and its regional proxies, including Houthi forces in Yemen, are bracing for potential attacks. An unclassified intelligence memorandum from Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton to Secretary of State Marco Rubio recently highlighted that Iranian targeting efforts against American personnel have reached advanced stages in multiple regions.

Regional Precaution and Force Protection

Anticipating immediate retaliation from Tehran if strikes commence, Washington has begun taking steps to mitigate risk to American personnel across the region. Nonessential military troop rotations to the Middle East have been put on hold, and the State Department is quietly reducing nonessential diplomatic staff across several regional missions following an ordered departure at the U.S. Embassy in Riyadh.

At the same time, U.S. naval assets remain actively engaged in key maritime choke points. CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper recently completed an aerial assessment of the Strait of Hormuz, where U.S. naval forces continue enforcing maritime security and escorting commercial shipping past Iranian naval patrols.

Coordination with Israeli Strategic Objectives

The strategic timeline is also closely aligned with Israeli military planning. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has reportedly urged Washington to support aggressive strikes targeting the Iranian regime's core apparatus.

While Israeli leadership initially sought an immediate joint operation, senior American officials—including Trump—have requested that Israel delay coordinated action until after the U.S. midterms. The postponement is intended to allow for full joint operational integration and ensure robust defensive coverage for Israel against expected Iranian missile counterattacks.
